CFML Language Reference: Functions

IsAuthorized

Checks the security policies of the user's security context to see whether the authenticated user is allowed to use a resource, optionally for a particular action.

Category

Authentication functions

Syntax

IsAuthorized(resourcetype, resourcename [, action ])

Parameters

resourcetype
The kind of resource: Application, CFML, File, DataSource, Component, Collection, CustomTag or UserObject.
resourcename
The name of the resource as entered in the security rule. A rule ending in * matches any name that starts with the text before it.
action
The action to check, such as Read, Write or Delete for a File. If omitted, any action covered by a rule counts.

Returns

YES if a policy grants the user the resource (and action), NO otherwise.

Usage

The user must first be authenticated with CFAUTHENTICATE; for anybody else the function returns NO. Rules and policies are defined per security context on the Advanced Security pages of the Administrator. Without Advanced Security configured, the answer is always NO, so keep a sensible fallback in your page.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Checks = "Application|Payroll|,File|/reports/salaries.txt|Read,DataSource|cfsnippets|Delete">
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Type</TH><TH>Resource</TH><TH>Action</TH><TH>IsAuthorized</TH></TR>
<CFLOOP LIST="#Checks#" INDEX="c">
  <CFSET Type = ListGetAt(c, 1, "|")>
  <CFSET Res = ListGetAt(c, 2, "|")>
  <CFSET Act = "">
  <CFIF ListLen(c, "|") GT 2><CFSET Act = ListGetAt(c, 3, "|")></CFIF>
  <CFOUTPUT><TR><TD>#Type#</TD><TD>#Res#</TD><TD>#Act#&nbsp;</TD>
  <TD>#IsAuthorized(Type, Res, Act)#</TD></TR></CFOUTPUT>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
<CFIF NOT IsAuthenticated()>
  <P><I>Nobody is logged in, so every answer is NO.</I></P>
</CFIF>

See also
